messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate from prefix group 'user-prefix-*' (errors spiked at 00:12 UTC). Auto-escalation triggered to #incidents and paging maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): seeing it, joining. Any initial suspicion?

harry: looks correlated with eviction churn on KV cache for that prefix pattern. Logs show frequent TTL evictions + downstream DB read spikes.

jordan: confirming hotkey-ish behavior — small set of prefixes with large QPS. KV backend hit rate dropped to ~10% for those prefixes.

sam-sre: can we temporarily bypass prefix cache for correctness while we throttle traffic? Need to avoid corrupted responses.

maya (oncall): prioritize correctness. Sam, can you outline mitigation steps?

sam-sre: propose immediate steps: 1) apply per-tenant rate cap for the offending tenants (soft cap 100 rps) 2) disable prefetch/pinned cache warming for prefix pattern 3) enable KV bypass for affected prefixes (fall back to authoritative storage) 4) increase eviction threshold to reduce churn.

eva: +1 on bypass for correctness, but that will increase DB load. Need traffic shaping first.

maya (oncall): harry — can you run a quick traffic split to route 20% of traffic for those prefixes to a canary pool with KV bypass and reduced concurrency?

harry: doing. Command:
```bash
# route 20% of prefix user-prefix-{A..Z} to canary pool
infractl route split --prefix "user-prefix-*" --to canary-bypass:20
```

ops-bot: CONFIRMATION: route split job queued (job id: rts-240512-1). Estimated apply in 14s.

jordan: also applying immediate quota trim for tenants t-867 and t-901. Reducing burst windows to 60s and throttling to 120 rps.

sam-sre: enabling KV bypass for prefix pattern now. Patch applied to runtime config: `prefix_kv_bypass = ["user-prefix-*"]`

eva: monitoring DB read QPS — set up temporary read-scaling autoscale to absorb extra load.

maya (oncall): customer-comms, prepare a short status note and DM the top 5 affected customers. Mention temporary throttling and correctness-first approach.

customer-comms: drafting. Short note: "We’re currently mitigating a traffic surge impacting a subset of tenants. To protect correctness we’ve temporarily adjusted caching and applied rate limits. Response quality preserved; latency may be higher. No data loss. We’ll update in 30m or on change."

harry: route split applied. Canary pool showing reduced error rate for canary traffic (5xx down from 6.2% -> 0.9%). Main fleet still at ~3.8% though.

sam-sre: KV bypass worked — correctness errors cleared on canary. Rest of fleet error signal likely from eviction churn causing partial stale lookups.

eva: DB autoscale is holding at +30% capacity. No saturation alerts so far.

maya (oncall): next steps: 1) keep canary active and increase to 40% if stable, 2) tune eviction threshold on main fleet, 3) prepare rollback plan to re-enable prefetch once stable.

jordan: I’ll increment eviction threshold from 2k keys->8k keys for that instance group. Applying hotpatch now.

ops-bot: HOTPATCH: eviction_threshold updated on group-42 (change id hp-240512-4).

harry: main fleet error rate dropped to 1.3% after threshold bump.

maya (oncall): good. Gradually ramp canary to 60% over next 10 minutes, observe DB and tail latency.

sam-sre: increasing canary to 60%: infractl route split --prefix "user-prefix-*" --to canary-bypass:60 --step 20 --wait 120s

customer-comms: status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "Mitigation in progress: cache bypass and traffic shaping applied for affected prefixes. Error rates improving; latency elevated for some requests. We will post another update in 30m."

eva: tail p50/p95 latency up ~80ms/420ms for bypassed requests; acceptable for now.

maya (oncall): prepare to hand off after 30m check-in. Assign next oncall: harry.

harry: taking over post-checkin. I’ll keep a watch for rollback windows and customer DMs.

maya (oncall): final notes before handoff: - correctness preserved by bypass - DB autoscale in place - main fleet updated with higher eviction thresholds - canary ramp to 60% successful - customer-comms posted. If anything regresses, revert routing and re-enable prefetch off.

sam-sre: logging mitigation actions for postmortem. Will include metrics, commands, and timestamps.

maya (oncall): thanks team. handing off to harry for monitoring & postmortem. paging resolved for me. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged closed for maya (oncall) at 00:56 UTC.
